trapezium bone: Lateral bone of the distal row; with the 1st metacarpal it forms the saddle joint that allows opposition of the thumb.
trapezoid bone: The smallest bone of the distal row; articulates with the base of the 2nd metacarpal.
trapezoid ligament: Lateral, quadrilateral part of the coracoclavicular ligament; prevents the scapula sliding medially under the clavicle.
trapezoid line: Line on the lower surface of the lateral end; the trapezoid part of the coracoclavicular ligament attaches to it.
trapezoideocapitate interosseous ligamen: Interosseous ligament between the trapezoid and capitate.
triangular fovea: Upper pit on the anterolateral surface of the arytenoid; it contains glandular tissue.
triceps brachii muscle: The only elbow extensor, whose long, lateral and medial heads insert into the olecranon. Radial nerve; triceps reflex C7.
triceps surae muscle: Muscle group made up of the two heads of gastrocnemius and soleus; inserting into the calcaneus via the Achilles tendon, it plantarflexes the foot. Tibial nerve (S1–S2).
triquetrocapitate ligament: Binds the triquetrum to the capitate.
triquetrohamate ligament: Binds the triquetrum to the hamate; contributes to midcarpal stability.
triquetrum bone: Pyramid-shaped medial bone of the proximal row; articulates with the pisiform on its palmar surface.
triradiate cartilage: Y-shaped growth cartilage joining the ilium, ischium and pubis in the acetabulum in childhood; it ossifies at puberty.
trochanteric bursa of gluteus maximus mu: Between the iliotibial band and the greater trochanter; trochanteric bursitis most often occurs here.
trochanteric bursa of gluteus medius mus: Bursae beneath the gluteus medius tendon.
trochanteric bursa of gluteus minimus mu: Bursa beneath the gluteus minimus tendon.
trochanteric fossa: Fossa on the medial surface of the greater trochanter; obturator externus inserts here.
trochanteric insertion: Common insertion area of the deep hip rotators around the greater trochanter.
trochlea of humerus: Pulley-shaped articular surface at the lower medial end of the humerus; forms the hinge joint with the ulna.
trochlea of phalanx of foot: Pulley-shaped distal head of a toe phalanx; forms a hinge joint with the next phalanx.
trochlea of phalanx of hand: Pulley-shaped head of a finger phalanx; forms the interphalangeal hinge joint.
trochlea of superior oblique muscle: Fibrocartilaginous pulley at the superomedial corner of the orbit; the superior oblique tendon turns through it.
trochlea of talus: Pulley that sits in the mortise between the tibia and fibula; being wider in front, the joint is stable in dorsiflexion.
trochlear fovea: Pit at the superomedial corner of the orbit; the trochlea of superior oblique attaches here.
trochlear notch: Large notch that grips the trochlea of the humerus.
trochlear spine: Small spine in the trochlear fovea; holds the pulley of superior oblique.
tubercle of iliotibial tract: Prominence on the lateral condyle (Gerdy's tubercle); the iliotibial band inserts here.
tubercle of rib: Prominence behind the junction of the neck and shaft; articulates with the transverse process.
tubercle of scaphoid bone: Prominence on the palmar side of the scaphoid; the flexor retinaculum attaches to it, and it is felt at the front of the wrist.
tubercle of trapezium bone: Prominence on the palmar side of the trapezium; the FCR tendon passes in the groove beside it.
tuberculum sellae: Elevation in front of the hypophysial fossa.
tuberosity for coracoclavicular ligament: Lower lateral surface of the clavicle; both parts of the coracoclavicular ligament attach here.
tuberosity of cuboid bone: Ridge on the plantar surface of the cuboid; the fibularis longus tendon passes in the groove in front of it.
tuberosity of distal phalanx of foot: Tuberosity of distal phalanx of foot
Rough expansion at the tip of a distal toe phalanx; supports the soft tissue of the toe tip.
tuberosity of distal phalanx of hand: Tuberosity of distal phalanx of hand
Expansion at the tip of a distal finger phalanx; supports the finger pulp and nail bed.
tuberosity of navicular bone: Projection on the medial surface of the navicular; the main insertion of tibialis posterior.
tuberosity of ulna: Rough area below the coronoid process; brachialis inserts here.
twelfth rib: 12th rib: a floating rib; its front end is free and ends among the muscles of the abdominal wall.
tympanic part of temporal bone: Part forming the bony wall of the external acoustic meatus.
ulna: Forearm bone on the little finger (medial) side; with the olecranon and coronoid process it grips the trochlea of the humerus to form the elbow joint.
ulnar collateral ligament: Spreads like a triangular fan from the medial epicondyle to the ulna; resists valgus stress and tears in baseball pitchers.
ulnar collateral ligament of wrist joint: Ligament from the ulnar styloid process to the triquetrum and pisiform.
ulnar head of extensor carpi ulnaris: Ulnar head of extensor carpi ulnaris
Arises from the posterior border of the ulna; the muscle inserts into the base of the 5th metacarpal, extending and ulnarly deviating the hand.
ulnar head of flexor carpi ulnaris: Ulnar head of flexor carpi ulnaris
Arises from the olecranon and the posterior border of the ulna; the muscle inserts into the pisiform, flexing and ulnarly deviating the hand. Ulnar nerve.
ulnar notch: Notch at the lower end of the radius; forms the distal radio-ulnar joint with the ulnar head.
ulnar styloid process: Process at the posteromedial end of the ulnar head; the articular disc attaches to it.
ulnocapitate ligament: Palmar ligament running from the ulnar side to the capitate.
ulnolunate ligament: Palmar ligament running from the TFCC to the lunate.
ulnopisiform ligament: Small ligament between the ulna and pisiform.
ulnotriquetral ligament: Palmar ligament running from the TFCC to the triquetrum.
uncinate process of first thoracic verte: Small process on the body of T1 resembling those of the cervical vertebrae.
uncinate process of vertebra: Process on the upper lateral edge of a cervical vertebral body; it forms the uncovertebral (Luschka) joint, and osteophytes here can compress nerve roots.
upper canine: Tooth at the corner of the mouth with the longest root; tears food. The root of the upper canine can reach up to the corner of the eye.
upper first molar tooth: The first permanent tooth to erupt (age 6); it has a broad chewing surface and three roots.
upper first premolar: Premolar with two cusps; begins crushing food. In the upper jaw it usually has two roots.
upper lateral incisor: Single-rooted incisor next to the central incisor.
upper medial incisor: Sharp-edged, single-rooted middle front tooth; cuts food by biting. It erupts at 6–8 years in the permanent dentition.
upper second molar tooth: Second molar erupting around age 12; it grinds food.
upper second premolar: Second premolar; usually single-rooted, with no counterpart in the milk teeth (it replaces the milk molars).
